advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge the exception's existing sanitized `.diagnostic` (if any) into the outcome diagnostic built by `_agentic_outcome.fixed`
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:381-383: `def fixed(cls ...): diagnostic = {"exception_type": type(exc).__name__}; return _failure.LLMOutcome(cls, diagnostic, retryable=cls in _failure._RETRYABLE)`
src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:82: `budget_err.diagnostic = budget_diag` (run_shape counters attached to LLMBudgetExhaustedError)
src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:94: `exc.diagnostic = merged` (RunawayToolLoopError's merged repetition diagnostic)
src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:441: `**_failure.resolution_fields(outcome)` writes `outcome.diagnostic` onto the degraded verdict's coverage
advisory.finding: When `_agentic_outcome` classifies an LLMBudgetExhaustedError, RunawayToolLoopError or a truncation, it builds a fresh LLMOutcome whose diagnostic is only `{"exception_type": ...}`. It drops the run-shape diagnostic that run_failure already attached to the exception (request counts, limits, repetition summary). So the degraded verdict's `coverage.diagnostic` and the log_degrade session-log entry lose the counters an operator needs to act on FIX_AGENT_DESIGN or CHANGE_SETTINGS.
scenarios: The agentic review hits its 60/156 tool-step budget. The verdict says FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, but its diagnostic has only `exception_type`, so nothing shows which limit tripped or which tool call repeated.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `fixed`, build the diagnostic as `{**_failure.sanitize_diagnostic(getattr(exc, 'diagnostic', None) or {}), 'exception_type': type(exc).__name__}`, or an equivalent that keeps the run_shape counters.

tests/unit/test_refusal_as_content.py:29-30 and 69-72 only check `pytest.raises(UnretryableOutputError)`; searching tests/ for `stop_reason` turns up no assertion on the raised error's `.stop_reason` attribute

advisory.finding: The new `err.stop_reason = ...` stamping in structured.check_stop_reason and check_response is never exercised by a test. The failure-class tests that depend on it build the exception and set `stop_reason` by hand, so removing the production stamping keeps every test green. Meanwhile a real refusal would silently fall back to NEEDS_INVESTIGATION with input_rejected=False.
scenarios: `structured.check_stop_reason("refusal")` raising an error whose `.stop_reason` is None: no test fails, yet agentic_failure_error then classifies a real refusal as NEEDS_INVESTIGATION instead of CHANGE_INPUT + input_rejected
`structured.check_response(_resp(finish_reason="stop", provider_details={"refusal": "..."}))` must stamp `stop_reason == "refusal"`; this is untested
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_refusal_as_content.py (or test_structured.py), capture `with pytest.raises(UnretryableOutputError) as ei:` and assert `ei.value.stop_reason == reason`. For `provider_details={"refusal": ...}` with finish_reason "stop", assert `ei.value.stop_reason == "refusal"`. For a retries-exhausted UnretryableOutputError, assert `stop_reason is None`.

advisory.finding: The plan-review.yaml now passes the DET floor's det_advisory, det_coverage and det_blocking, plus the agent's provider_provenance, into plan_review_agentic_verdict. No test asserts that any of them reach the adapted verdict. Every agentic test filters the advisory list down to `tier == "AGENTIC"`, and none checks `coverage.det` or provider_provenance, so dropping that wiring (or the adapter's merge) would go undetected.
scenarios: The yaml `det_advisory:` line is removed or misnamed: DET advisories vanish from agentic verdicts while every test stays green

Assert the DET findings appear in advisory/blocking, the verdict is BLOCK, `coverage["det"] == det_coverage`, and the provenance is carried. End to end, assert the agentic verdict's `tier == "DET"` advisories equal the pipeline verdict's for the same description.
